best_for: Developers and freelancers who track time against Jira, GitHub or GitLab tickets and want a to-do list with timers that keeps data on their own machine.

points.title: No account, no paid tier
points.text: All features are free on all platforms, with no premium tier. It needs no account and works offline.

points.title: Time tracking is built in
points.text: Each task can run a timer, with a Pomodoro mode, timesheets and reports. Tasks show as lists, a Kanban board or an Eisenhower matrix, and a schedule planner can import your calendar.

points.title: Pulls tickets from your tracker
points.text: It can import issues assigned to you from Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Trello, Linear, ClickUp, OpenProject, Redmine, Nextcloud Deck and Azure DevOps. Time logged can go back to Jira, GitLab, OpenProject and Redmine as worklogs.

points.title: Sync is opt-in
points.text: Data stays on your device unless you turn on sync. Options are SuperSync, which is end-to-end encrypted and can be self-hosted, Dropbox or WebDAV. The project says the app collects no data.

points.title: Mac needs macOS 13
points.text: The Mac disk images, for Intel and Apple Silicon, need macOS 13 or later. Windows gets x64 and ARM64 installers.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is x64 only
points.text: Flathub marks the Flatpak as verified, published by Johannes Millan, but it is built for x64 only; a Snap is also offered. The Windows listing keeps 138 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
